subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology

clinical_case_questions.q: A 26-year-old primigravida presents at 11 weeks by a reliable LMP. Her cycles were regular at 28 days. Which method is most appropriate for calculating the estimated date of delivery?
clinical_case_questions.e: For a regular 28-day cycle, EDD is estimated by LMP + 9 months + 7 days (or 280 days). First-trimester CRL ultrasound is the most accurate dating method when LMP is uncertain or dates are discordant.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: Naegele rule = LMP + 9 months + 7 days for a 28-day cycle.
Incorrect: adding 6 months is not a standard EDD method.
Incorrect: quickening is variable and less accurate for dating.
Incorrect: fundal height is a screening estimate, not the best dating method.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 30-week pregnant woman has BP 166/112 mmHg on repeat measurement, headache and proteinuria. Which drug is used to prevent eclamptic seizures?
clinical_case_questions.e: Severe pre-eclampsia with neurological symptoms requires urgent maternal stabilisation, treatment of severe hypertension and magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis; plan delivery after stabilisation according to gestation and maternal-fetal status.
optionBuzzwords: Phenytoin is not first-line seizure prophylaxis in pre-eclampsia.
Correct: magnesium sulfate reduces risk of eclampsia and treats eclamptic seizures.
Diazepam is not routine prophylaxis and is not preferred over magnesium sulfate.
Levetiracetam is not standard first-line prophylaxis for eclampsia.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with eclampsia is receiving magnesium sulfate. Which clinical finding is the earliest useful bedside warning of magnesium toxicity?
clinical_case_questions.e: Loss of patellar/deep tendon reflexes is an early clinical sign of magnesium toxicity. Also monitor respiratory rate, urine output and renal function. Stop magnesium and give IV calcium gluconate for significant toxicity.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: absent DTRs are an early warning sign.
Jaundice is not a typical early sign of magnesium toxicity.
Tinnitus is not the characteristic monitoring sign.
Hyperactive bowel sounds are not a recognised toxicity marker.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 34-week pregnant woman with severe pre-eclampsia has epigastric pain, thrombocytopenia, raised AST/ALT and evidence of haemolysis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: HELLP = haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets; it is a severe pre-eclampsia spectrum disorder. Stabilise the mother, control BP/seizure risk and expedite delivery when indicated.
optionBuzzwords: Acute fatty liver may cause liver failure, hypoglycaemia and coagulopathy; haemolysis/low platelets pattern suggests HELLP.
Correct: haemolysis + elevated liver enzymes + low platelets.
TTP can cause MAHA and thrombocytopenia but does not classically produce the HELLP obstetric pattern.
Cholestasis causes pruritus and raised bile acids, not this triad.

clinical_case_questions.q: A pregnant woman at 26 weeks has a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test with 2-hour plasma glucose of 162 mg/dL using IADPSG criteria. How should this result be interpreted?
o: Overt diabetes only if fasting glucose is >200 mg/dL
Impaired glucose tolerance unrelated to pregnancy
clinical_case_questions.e: With a 75-g OGTT, a 2-hour value ≥153 mg/dL meets the IADPSG threshold for GDM (one abnormal value is sufficient). Apply the locally adopted national protocol where it differs.
optionBuzzwords: Incorrect: 162 mg/dL exceeds the IADPSG 2-hour threshold.
Correct: 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL meets IADPSG GDM criteria.
Incorrect: overt diabetes has separate diagnostic thresholds; this result already meets GDM criteria.
Incorrect: this is a pregnancy-specific diagnostic threshold, not an unrelated finding.

clinical_case_questions.q: An unsensitised RhD-negative pregnant woman delivers an RhD-positive baby. Within what interval should postpartum anti-D immunoglobulin ideally be administered?
o: Only if the next pregnancy is planned
clinical_case_questions.e: Give anti-D to eligible unsensitised RhD-negative women after delivery of an RhD-positive infant, ideally within 72 hours. Dose and additional fetomaternal haemorrhage testing follow local protocol.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: ideally within 72 hours; give as soon as possible if delayed.
Six weeks is too late for the standard postpartum window.
Prevention is important regardless of immediate future pregnancy plans.
Six months is far beyond the recommended interval.

clinical_case_questions.q: A dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy is identified on first-trimester ultrasound. Which sonographic sign supports dichorionicity?
o: Single placental mass always proves monochorionicity
clinical_case_questions.e: The lambda/twin-peak sign at the placental insertion supports dichorionicity. A thin T-sign is characteristic of monochorionic diamniotic twins. First-trimester chorionicity assessment is most reliable.
optionBuzzwords: T-sign supports monochorionic diamniotic pregnancy.
Correct: lambda/twin-peak sign supports dichorionicity.
Absence of a membrane suggests monoamniotic twins, not dichorionicity.
A single placental mass may represent fused dichorionic placentas; assess membrane insertion and placental layers.

clinical_case_questions.q: A fetus is at the 5th centile for estimated fetal weight at 32 weeks. Umbilical artery Doppler shows absent end-diastolic flow. Which statement is most appropriate?
o: This is a reassuring normal finding
This indicates significant placental vascular resistance and requires urgent specialist surveillance
It is diagnostic of congenital infection
clinical_case_questions.e: Estimated fetal weight below the 10th centile raises concern for FGR/SGA. Absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery indicates increased placental resistance and is associated with adverse perinatal risk; manage in a specialist unit with gestation-specific surveillance and delivery planning.
clinical_case_questions.b: This indicates significant placental vascular resistance and requires urgent specialist surveillance
optionBuzzwords: Incorrect: absent end-diastolic flow is abnormal and high risk.
Correct: it reflects severe placental vascular resistance and needs specialist management.
Fetal anaemia is assessed with middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity, not this finding.
Congenital infection requires targeted maternal/fetal evaluation; this Doppler is not diagnostic.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 31-week pregnant woman has painless vaginal bleeding. The uterus is soft and non-tender and fetal heart activity is present. What is the most likely diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Painless bleeding with a soft, non-tender uterus suggests placenta praevia. Avoid digital vaginal examination until placental location is known; confirm with ultrasound and stabilise the mother.
optionBuzzwords: Abruption typically causes painful bleeding, uterine tenderness/hypertonus; bleeding may be concealed.
Correct: classically painless antepartum haemorrhage with soft uterus.
Uterine rupture often presents with pain, maternal instability and fetal compromise, especially with scar.
Vasa praevia causes fetal bleeding after membrane rupture with acute fetal bradycardia.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 35-week pregnant woman develops sudden abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding and a tense tender uterus. Fetal heart rate is abnormal. Most likely diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Painful bleeding, uterine tenderness/tonicity and fetal compromise strongly suggest placental abruption. Maternal resuscitation and rapid assessment of maternal-fetal status are priorities; bleeding can be concealed.
optionBuzzwords: Placenta praevia is classically painless with a soft uterus.
Correct: painful bleeding + tender hypertonic uterus = abruption.
Cervical ectropion causes minor contact bleeding, not maternal-fetal compromise.
Show is blood-stained mucus associated with cervical change, not a tense tender uterus.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman has heavy bleeding immediately after vaginal delivery. The uterus is enlarged and boggy. What is the first-line uterotonic for atonic postpartum haemorrhage?
clinical_case_questions.e: Atonic PPH is managed simultaneously with uterine massage, calling for help, resuscitation, IV access/blood products as needed and uterotonics. Oxytocin is first-line; escalate according to contraindications and protocol, and consider tranexamic acid early within 3 hours of birth.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: oxytocin is first-line uterotonic for atonic PPH.
Magnesium sulfate is an anticonvulsant in pre-eclampsia and may worsen uterine atony.
Ritodrine is a beta-agonist tocolytic and is not used to treat PPH.
Mifepristone is an antiprogestin, not an acute PPH uterotonic.

clinical_case_questions.q: After delivery, a woman continues to bleed despite a well-contracted uterus. Examination reveals retained placental tissue. Which component of the 4 Ts is responsible?
clinical_case_questions.e: The 4 Ts of PPH are Tone (atony), Trauma (genital tract injury), Tissue (retained placenta/products) and Thrombin (coagulopathy). A contracted uterus with retained tissue points to Tissue.
optionBuzzwords: Tone refers to uterine atony; the uterus here is contracted.
Trauma includes cervical/vaginal/perineal tears or uterine rupture.
Correct: retained placental tissue = Tissue.
Thrombin refers to coagulation disorders.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman at 33 weeks has regular painful contractions and cervical change. Membranes are intact. Which intervention reduces neonatal respiratory distress if delivery is expected within 7 days?
clinical_case_questions.e: Antenatal corticosteroids (e.g., betamethasone) are given when preterm birth is likely within 7 days in the appropriate gestational window. Magnesium sulfate may be used for fetal neuroprotection at earlier gestations according to protocol; tocolysis may provide time for steroids/transfer if safe.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: corticosteroids accelerate fetal lung maturation and reduce neonatal morbidity.
Antibiotics are indicated for specific reasons such as GBS prophylaxis or PPROM, not all intact-membrane preterm labour.
Tocolysis is short-term and not continued routinely until 37 weeks.
Magnesium sulfate is not a surfactant; it may provide fetal neuroprotection.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman at 30 weeks reports a gush of fluid. Sterile speculum examination shows pooling and ferning. She is afebrile with reassuring fetal status. What is the diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: PPROM is rupture of membranes before onset of labour and before 37 weeks. Confirm clinically with sterile speculum examination; avoid unnecessary digital examinations. Management depends on gestation, infection, labour and fetal status, with antibiotics/corticosteroids as indicated.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: rupture before labour and <37 weeks = PPROM.
Placenta praevia causes bleeding, not pooling/ferning of liquor.
Urine may mimic fluid loss but does not produce amniotic-fluid ferning.
Leukorrhoea is discharge, not a gush with pooling/ferning.

clinical_case_questions.q: During vaginal delivery, the fetal head delivers but then retracts against the perineum (“turtle sign”). What is the first manoeuvre?
o: Immediate forceful traction on the fetal head
clinical_case_questions.e: Turtle sign indicates shoulder dystocia. Call for help, stop pushing briefly, perform McRoberts manoeuvre and apply suprapubic pressure. Avoid fundal pressure and excessive traction.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure are first-line manoeuvres.
Fundal pressure worsens impaction and is contraindicated.
Excessive traction risks brachial plexus injury.
Internal podalic version is not the first manoeuvre for shoulder dystocia.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with one previous low-transverse caesarean is counselled about trial of labour after caesarean. Which history is a major contraindication to planned TOLAC?
clinical_case_questions.e: A previous classical incision or prior uterine rupture is a major contraindication to planned TOLAC because of uterine rupture risk. Individual candidacy depends on scar type, obstetric history, facility and informed consent.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: classical incision involves the contractile upper segment and carries high rupture risk.
Previous vaginal birth generally improves the chance of VBAC success.
Singleton cephalic presentation is generally favourable.
Spontaneous labour is generally associated with a higher VBAC success rate than induction.

clinical_case_questions.q: A labouring woman is 6 cm dilated. The fetal head is at -2 station and the cervix has not changed over 4 hours despite adequate contractions. Which concept should guide assessment?
clinical_case_questions.e: Active labour is generally considered from 6 cm. Active-phase arrest is diagnosed only when there is no cervical change despite adequate uterine activity for at least 4 hours, or inadequate activity for at least 6 hours, with ruptured membranes under commonly used criteria. Assess the full clinical context and local guideline.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: at 6 cm, evaluate active-phase arrest criteria, not older 4-cm thresholds.
At 6 cm she is in active labour, not latent phase.
Second stage begins at full dilatation.
Descent after delivery is irrelevant.

clinical_case_questions.q: A postpartum woman develops fever, uterine tenderness and foul-smelling lochia on day 3 after caesarean delivery. Most likely diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Postpartum endometritis presents with fever, uterine/fundal tenderness and foul lochia, especially after caesarean delivery. Start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics according to local protocol and assess for retained products or sepsis.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: fever + uterine tenderness + foul lochia suggests endometritis.
Mastitis causes breast pain, erythema and fever.
Stress incontinence does not cause fever or uterine tenderness.
Ovarian torsion causes acute pelvic pain, not foul lochia.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 24-year-old has oligomenorrhoea, hirsutism and acne. Pregnancy test is negative. Which is required before diagnosing PCOS?
o: Exclude important mimics such as thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia and non-classic CAH
clinical_case_questions.e: PCOS is diagnosed using accepted criteria after excluding mimics. In adults, two of ovulatory dysfunction, clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology (or validated AMH alternative in appropriate guidance) may establish diagnosis. LH:FSH ratio and obesity are not required.
clinical_case_questions.b: Exclude important mimics such as thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia and non-classic CAH
optionBuzzwords: Correct: exclude mimics including thyroid dysfunction, hyperprolactinaemia and non-classic CAH when indicated.
CT is not required and is not the preferred modality.
Lean women can have PCOS.
LH:FSH ratio is neither necessary nor sufficiently reliable diagnostically.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with primary amenorrhoea, normal breast development, scant pubic hair and a short blind-ending vagina. Uterus is absent. Karyotype is 46,XX. Most likely diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: MRKH is uterovaginal agenesis in a 46,XX individual with normal ovarian function and secondary sexual characteristics. Renal and skeletal anomalies may coexist. Complete androgen insensitivity is 46,XY and often has sparse pubic/axillary hair.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: 46,XX, normal breasts, absent uterus and short vagina suggest MRKH.
CAIS is 46,XY with testes and typically sparse pubic/axillary hair.
Turner syndrome commonly has streak ovaries and impaired secondary sexual development.
Imperforate hymen causes outflow obstruction with a uterus present and often cyclic pain/hematocolpos.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 16-year-old has cyclic lower abdominal pain, primary amenorrhoea and a tense bluish bulging hymen. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Imperforate hymen causes outflow obstruction, cyclic pain and haematocolpos/haematometra. A bulging bluish hymen is classic; treat with appropriate surgical opening after assessment.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: cyclic pain + bulging bluish hymen = imperforate hymen.
MRKH has absent uterus/vagina and does not cause haematocolpos behind a hymen.
Gonadal dysgenesis causes absent/poor puberty, not obstructed menstrual flow.
Cervical cancer is not a likely diagnosis in this adolescent presentation.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 28-year-old with infertility has severe dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia and a fixed retroverted uterus. Ultrasound shows a homogeneous “ground-glass” ovarian cyst. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Endometriosis causes dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia and infertility. An ovarian endometrioma often has homogeneous low-level “ground-glass” echoes on ultrasound.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: endometrioma produces ground-glass echoes.
Dermoid often shows echogenic components, shadowing or fat-fluid level.
Serous cystadenoma is typically anechoic/simple cystic, not classic ground-glass.
PCOS produces multiple small follicles and endocrine/ovulatory features.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 36-year-old has heavy menstrual bleeding and an enlarged irregularly contoured uterus. Ultrasound shows well-circumscribed whorled myometrial masses. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Leiomyomas are benign smooth-muscle tumours, often producing an irregularly enlarged uterus and whorled hypoechoic myometrial masses. Symptoms depend on size and location.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: whorled myometrial masses and irregular uterus suggest fibroids.
Adenomyosis more often causes a uniformly enlarged boggy tender uterus and myometrial heterogeneity.
Endometrial polyp is an intracavitary focal lesion.
Endometrial carcinoma is a malignant endometrial lesion, not whorled myometrial masses.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 48-year-old with obesity and chronic anovulation presents with abnormal uterine bleeding. Which investigation is particularly important to exclude endometrial hyperplasia or malignancy?
clinical_case_questions.e: Endometrial sampling is indicated in abnormal uterine bleeding at age ≥45 years and in younger patients with risk factors such as chronic anovulation, obesity or persistent bleeding. Tailor to local guidelines and clinical context.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: endometrial biopsy/sampling assesses hyperplasia and malignancy.
CA-125 is not a screening or exclusion test for endometrial cancer.
HSG assesses uterine cavity/tubal patency in infertility.
Laparoscopy does not sample the endometrium and is not first-line here.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 27-year-old with infertility has bilateral tubal block on HSG and a history of pelvic inflammatory disease. Which organism is a common cause of PID-associated tubal damage?
clinical_case_questions.e: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae are major causes of PID. Subclinical infection can cause salpingitis, adhesions, ectopic pregnancy and tubal-factor infertility.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: C. trachomatis is a major cause of PID and tubal scarring.
Candida causes vulvovaginitis, not typical ascending PID.
Gardnerella is associated with bacterial vaginosis; it is not the classic sole cause of PID.
Treponema pallidum causes syphilis, not typical PID.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman has frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge, vulvovaginal irritation and a “strawberry cervix”. Wet mount shows motile flagellated organisms. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Trichomoniasis is caused by Trichomonas vaginalis. Frothy yellow-green discharge, strawberry cervix and motile flagellates are classic. Treat patient and sexual partners; advise abstinence until treatment is complete.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: motile flagellates + strawberry cervix = trichomoniasis.
Candida causes thick curdy discharge and pseudohyphae/yeast.
BV causes thin homogeneous discharge, fishy odour and clue cells.
Herpes causes painful vesicles/ulcers, not motile flagellates.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 32-year-old has thin homogeneous vaginal discharge with fishy odour. Vaginal pH is 5.5 and microscopy shows clue cells. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Bacterial vaginosis is diagnosed clinically by Amsel criteria or Gram stain/Nugent score. Clue cells, pH >4.5, thin discharge and fishy odour are classic. Treat symptomatic patients and selected special situations per guideline.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: clue cells + elevated pH + fishy odour suggest BV.
Candida usually has normal pH and budding yeast/pseudohyphae.
Trichomoniasis may have elevated pH but motile trichomonads and frothy discharge.
Atrophic vaginitis occurs with hypoestrogenism and has pale thin mucosa.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 22-year-old has acute unilateral pelvic pain, vomiting and an adnexal mass. Doppler shows reduced ovarian blood flow. What is the next best management?
o: Urgent diagnostic laparoscopy and detorsion when feasible
Start combined oral contraceptive and review in 3 months
clinical_case_questions.e: Ovarian torsion is a surgical emergency. Doppler flow can be preserved despite torsion, so normal flow does not exclude it. Prompt laparoscopy with detorsion and ovarian preservation when possible is preferred.
clinical_case_questions.b: Urgent diagnostic laparoscopy and detorsion when feasible
optionBuzzwords: Correct: urgent surgery is needed to salvage the ovary.
Observation risks ovarian infarction and loss.
COCs do not treat acute torsion.
Antibiotics alone do not correct twisting of the adnexa.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 54-year-old woman has postmenopausal bleeding. Transvaginal ultrasound shows endometrial thickness of 8 mm. What is the next step?
o: Reassure because bleeding is common after menopause
clinical_case_questions.e: Postmenopausal bleeding requires evaluation for endometrial cancer. An endometrial thickness >4 mm in a woman with postmenopausal bleeding generally warrants endometrial sampling; persistent bleeding needs evaluation even with a thin stripe.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: 8 mm is above the usual 4-mm threshold in symptomatic postmenopausal bleeding.
Postmenopausal bleeding is abnormal until evaluated.
Pap smear screens cervical disease, not endometrial pathology.
Serum progesterone does not exclude endometrial malignancy.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 29-year-old has a cervical smear showing HSIL. What is the appropriate next step in evaluation?
clinical_case_questions.e: HSIL cytology carries significant risk of CIN2+ and requires prompt colposcopic evaluation with biopsy or an age/risk-appropriate expedited treatment pathway under current guidelines.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: colposcopy and histological assessment are indicated.
Five-year repeat is unsafe for HSIL.
CA-125 is an ovarian tumour marker, not a cervical dysplasia test.
Antifungals do not treat high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 45-year-old has a cervical lesion. Biopsy shows invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Which lymph nodes are commonly involved early in cervical cancer spread?
o: Pelvic nodes (obturator/internal and external iliac groups)
Inguinal nodes only in every case
Para-aortic nodes are always the first station
clinical_case_questions.e: Cervical cancer spreads locally and through lymphatics, commonly to parametrial and pelvic nodes including obturator and iliac groups; para-aortic involvement may occur with progression. Staging is clinical/imaging-informed according to FIGO guidance.
clinical_case_questions.b: Pelvic nodes (obturator/internal and external iliac groups)
optionBuzzwords: Correct: pelvic nodal groups are common early lymphatic stations.
Axillary nodes are not the usual regional drainage.
Inguinal nodes are more relevant to lower vaginal/vulval lesions.
Para-aortic nodes may be involved but are not always first.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 23-year-old has a unilateral ovarian mass. Histology shows Schiller-Duval bodies and serum AFP is elevated. Most likely tumour?
clinical_case_questions.e: Yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumour is a malignant germ-cell tumour of young women; Schiller-Duval bodies and elevated AFP are characteristic.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: Schiller-Duval bodies + AFP = yolk sac tumour.
Dysgerminoma is associated with LDH and large clear-cell tumour; occasional hCG.
Mature teratoma contains mature tissues from germ layers; no Schiller-Duval bodies.
Granulosa cell tumour may secrete inhibin/estrogen and show Call-Exner bodies.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 21-year-old has an ovarian mass. Histology shows large cells with clear cytoplasm and lymphocyte-rich septa. Which serum marker may be elevated?
clinical_case_questions.e: Dysgerminoma is the commonest malignant ovarian germ-cell tumour and may elevate LDH; it is radiosensitive and often presents in young women.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: LDH may be elevated in dysgerminoma.
AFP suggests yolk sac tumour, not dysgerminoma in every case.
CA 19-9 may be elevated in some mucinous/teratomatous lesions, not a characteristic marker.
CEA is not the characteristic marker.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 30-year-old has infertility and galactorrhoea. Serum prolactin is markedly elevated. Which mechanism explains anovulation?
clinical_case_questions.e: Hyperprolactinaemia suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility, reducing LH/FSH secretion and causing anovulation/amenorrhoea. Evaluate pregnancy, medications, thyroid function and pituitary causes.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: high prolactin suppresses GnRH pulsatility.
An appropriate LH surge is absent in anovulation.
Increased aromatisation is not the main mechanism.
FSH is not increased; gonadotropin drive is often reduced.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 26-year-old with infertility has a normal semen analysis and patent tubes. Mid-luteal progesterone is 2 ng/mL. What does this most strongly suggest?
o: Anovulation or inadequate luteal progesterone exposure
clinical_case_questions.e: A properly timed mid-luteal progesterone above the laboratory threshold (commonly >3 ng/mL) supports recent ovulation. A low value may reflect anovulation or mistimed sampling; interpret with cycle timing.
clinical_case_questions.b: Anovulation or inadequate luteal progesterone exposure
optionBuzzwords: Correct: low progesterone suggests anovulation or mistimed sample.
A value of 2 ng/mL does not confirm ovulation.
Tubal patency is a separate assessment.
Normal semen analysis does not indicate male factor infertility.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with primary infertility has a normal uterine cavity and patent tubes. Which test is the basic first-line evaluation of the male partner?
clinical_case_questions.e: Semen analysis is a first-line, non-invasive evaluation of male-factor infertility. Repeat abnormal results and assess the couple together; invasive tests are reserved for selected cases.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: semen analysis is the initial male evaluation.
Testicular biopsy is not a routine first-line test.
PSA evaluates prostate disease, not fertility.
CT is not routine first-line fertility testing.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 39-year-old with hot flushes and amenorrhoea for 14 months asks about menopause. Which hormonal pattern is expected?
clinical_case_questions.e: Menopause is diagnosed retrospectively after 12 months of amenorrhoea in the appropriate age group without another cause. Ovarian follicle depletion leads to low estradiol and elevated FSH.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: low ovarian estrogen feedback causes elevated FSH.
This pattern is opposite to menopause.
Progesterone is not persistently high after menopause.
AMH is low/undetectable with depleted ovarian reserve.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 31-year-old with symptomatic uterovaginal prolapse has descent of the cervix to the hymen but not beyond it. Which POP-Q stage is this?
clinical_case_questions.e: POP-Q stage II means the leading edge is within 1 cm proximal or distal to the hymen. Stage I is >1 cm above; stage III is >1 cm beyond but not complete eversion; stage IV is complete/near-complete eversion.
optionBuzzwords: Stage I: leading edge remains >1 cm above hymen.
Correct: leading edge lies within 1 cm of the hymen.
Stage III: >1 cm beyond hymen but not complete eversion.
Stage IV: complete/near-complete eversion.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with pelvic inflammatory disease has fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness and a complex adnexal mass. What complication should be suspected?
clinical_case_questions.e: A tubo-ovarian abscess is a severe PID complication presenting with fever, pelvic pain, adnexal tenderness/mass and systemic illness. Admit, give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and consider drainage/surgery if indicated.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: PID + fever + complex adnexal mass suggests TOA.
OHSS follows ovarian stimulation and causes enlarged ovaries/ascites, not PID signs.
Endometrioma is usually chronic and does not explain fever/systemic infection.
Fibroid degeneration causes focal uterine pain, not adnexal infectious mass.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 25-year-old has secondary amenorrhoea after severe postpartum haemorrhage. She cannot lactate and has low FSH, LH and estradiol. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Sheehan syndrome is postpartum pituitary ischaemic necrosis after severe haemorrhage/hypotension. Failure to lactate (low prolactin), amenorrhoea and hypopituitarism are classic clues.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: postpartum haemorrhage + agalactia + hypopituitarism = Sheehan syndrome.
Asherman causes intrauterine adhesions after uterine instrumentation; pituitary hormones are generally intact.
PCOS causes hyperandrogenism/ovulatory dysfunction, not agalactia after shock.
POI typically has elevated FSH, not low gonadotropins.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman develops scanty menses and infertility after repeated uterine curettage. Hysteroscopy shows intrauterine adhesions. Diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Asherman syndrome is intrauterine adhesions, commonly after curettage or uterine infection, causing hypomenorrhoea/amenorrhoea and infertility. Hysteroscopy is diagnostic and therapeutic.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: intrauterine synechiae after instrumentation = Asherman syndrome.
Sheehan is postpartum pituitary necrosis.
Adenomyosis causes heavy painful menses and a boggy uterus.
Cervical ectropion does not cause intrauterine adhesions.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 33-year-old with an intrauterine device in situ has a positive pregnancy test, unilateral pain and an empty uterus on transvaginal ultrasound. What diagnosis must be urgently excluded?
clinical_case_questions.e: Pregnancy with an IUD has a low absolute pregnancy risk, but if pregnancy occurs, the proportion that are ectopic is higher. Evaluate urgently with serial hCG and transvaginal ultrasound; haemodynamic instability requires emergency management.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: ectopic pregnancy must be actively excluded.
Molar pregnancy usually has characteristic intrauterine trophoblastic findings and very high hCG.
An empty uterus with pain and positive test requires pregnancy-of-unknown-location/ectopic evaluation, not assumption of miscarriage.
A cervical polyp does not explain this presentation.

clinical_case_questions.q: A haemodynamically stable woman has a confirmed unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, low beta-hCG, no fetal cardiac activity and reliable follow-up. Which treatment may be appropriate?
o: Methotrexate in a carefully selected patient
clinical_case_questions.e: Systemic methotrexate is an option for selected stable patients with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy who meet clinical, biochemical and imaging criteria and can comply with follow-up. Surgery is required for instability, rupture or contraindications/failure.
clinical_case_questions.b: Methotrexate in a carefully selected patient
optionBuzzwords: Correct: methotrexate may be used in appropriately selected stable cases.
Hysterectomy is not routine treatment for tubal ectopic pregnancy.
Oxytocin does not treat ectopic trophoblast.
Misoprostol alone is not standard treatment for tubal ectopic pregnancy.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman has a positive pregnancy test, vaginal bleeding and an ultrasound showing a gestational sac without embryo at a size meeting criteria for pregnancy failure. What is the safest principle before intervention?
o: Confirm nonviability using accepted ultrasound criteria or repeat scan when uncertain
Diagnose miscarriage from one borderline scan in all cases
clinical_case_questions.e: Early pregnancy failure should be diagnosed using validated conservative ultrasound criteria and/or repeat imaging when measurements are borderline. This avoids inadvertent interruption of a viable pregnancy.
clinical_case_questions.b: Confirm nonviability using accepted ultrasound criteria or repeat scan when uncertain
optionBuzzwords: Correct: use accepted criteria and repeat scan if uncertainty remains.
A single borderline scan may be inconclusive; avoid false-positive diagnosis.
Methotrexate is for selected ectopic pregnancy, not confirmed intrauterine miscarriage.
Hysterectomy is not treatment for early pregnancy loss.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with complete hydatidiform mole has very high beta-hCG, uterus larger than dates and bilateral theca-lutein cysts. Which genetic pattern is classically associated with a complete mole?
o: 69,XXY triploid conceptus with maternal and paternal sets
46,XY with one maternal and one paternal set
clinical_case_questions.e: Complete mole is usually diploid and androgenetic, commonly 46,XX (occasionally 46,XY), with nuclear DNA derived from paternal contribution. Partial mole is typically triploid with maternal and paternal sets.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: complete mole is classically androgenetic diploid 46,XX.
Triploidy with maternal and paternal sets is typical of partial mole.
45,X is Turner syndrome.
A biparental diploid conceptus is not the classic complete mole genotype.

clinical_case_questions.q: A patient with molar pregnancy undergoes suction evacuation. Which follow-up is essential to detect persistent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia?
clinical_case_questions.e: Serial quantitative beta-hCG surveillance after molar evacuation is essential until normalisation and for the recommended surveillance interval. Avoid pregnancy during surveillance because it confounds hCG interpretation.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: serial quantitative hCG detects persistent GTN.
CA-125 is not the marker for trophoblastic disease.
Colonoscopy is unrelated.
Clinical resolution does not exclude persistent trophoblastic tissue.

clinical_case_questions.q: A pregnant woman at 10 weeks has vaginal bleeding, a closed cervix and a viable intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound. What is the diagnosis?
clinical_case_questions.e: Threatened miscarriage is vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy with a closed cervical os and a viable intrauterine pregnancy. Counsel, assess Rh status and provide follow-up; management depends on history and local guidance.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: bleeding + closed os + viable pregnancy = threatened miscarriage.
Inevitable miscarriage usually has an open os and pregnancy loss is progressing.
Incomplete miscarriage has retained products and usually an open os.
Septic miscarriage has infection/systemic features.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with severe pre-eclampsia at 36 weeks is stabilised. What is the definitive treatment?
o: Delivery of the fetus and placenta after maternal stabilisation
Continue pregnancy until 40 weeks in every case
clinical_case_questions.e: Delivery is the definitive treatment for pre-eclampsia. Stabilise the mother, control severe BP, give magnesium sulfate when indicated and plan timing/mode of delivery based on gestation and maternal-fetal condition.
clinical_case_questions.b: Delivery of the fetus and placenta after maternal stabilisation
optionBuzzwords: Correct: delivery removes the placenta, the driver of pre-eclampsia.
Expectant management to 40 weeks is unsafe in severe disease.
Magnesium sulfate prevents seizures but does not cure pre-eclampsia.
ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy.

clinical_case_questions.q: A pregnant woman with asthma requires treatment for an acute exacerbation. Which statement is most appropriate?
o: Treat maternal asthma promptly; inhaled beta-agonist and systemic corticosteroids may be used when indicated
Withhold all bronchodilators because of pregnancy
Deliver immediately for every mild exacerbation
clinical_case_questions.e: Maternal hypoxia is dangerous to both mother and fetus. Treat asthma exacerbations promptly using standard therapies including inhaled bronchodilators and systemic corticosteroids when clinically indicated; monitor maternal oxygenation.
clinical_case_questions.b: Treat maternal asthma promptly; inhaled beta-agonist and systemic corticosteroids may be used when indicated
optionBuzzwords: Correct: prompt standard asthma treatment is appropriate in pregnancy.
Untreated bronchospasm/hypoxia poses greater risk than indicated inhaled therapy.
Mild exacerbation does not mandate delivery.
ACE inhibitors are not asthma treatment and are contraindicated in pregnancy.

clinical_case_questions.q: A pregnant woman at 29 weeks has severe iron-deficiency anaemia and cannot tolerate oral iron. Which treatment is appropriate after assessment?
o: Parenteral iron in the appropriate setting
clinical_case_questions.e: Parenteral iron may be considered in the second/third trimester when oral iron is not tolerated, ineffective or rapid correction is needed, after confirming iron deficiency and assessing risks. Transfusion is reserved for selected severe/symptomatic situations.
clinical_case_questions.b: Parenteral iron in the appropriate setting
optionBuzzwords: Correct: IV iron is an option when oral iron is unsuitable or inadequate.
Untreated severe iron deficiency increases maternal-fetal risk.
Erythropoietin is not routine for all pregnant patients with iron deficiency.
Folate alone does not correct iron deficiency.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman at 37 weeks has oligohydramnios with AFI 4 cm. Which fetal condition is classically associated with oligohydramnios in the second trimester?
clinical_case_questions.e: Fetal urine is the major source of amniotic fluid in the second half of pregnancy. Bilateral renal agenesis or severe urinary tract obstruction can cause oligohydramnios/anhydramnios.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: absent fetal kidneys markedly reduce fetal urine and liquor.
Maternal diabetes is associated more commonly with polyhydramnios.
Oesophageal atresia can impair swallowing and cause polyhydramnios.
Anencephaly may be associated with polyhydramnios due to impaired swallowing.

clinical_case_questions.q: A fetus has polyhydramnios and the mother has poorly controlled diabetes. Which mechanism contributes to excess amniotic fluid?
clinical_case_questions.e: Maternal hyperglycaemia causes fetal hyperglycaemia and osmotic diuresis, increasing fetal urine output and amniotic fluid volume. Evaluate for other causes including fetal anomalies.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: fetal osmotic diuresis increases urine output.
Reduced urine production causes oligohydramnios.
Placental infarction is not the usual mechanism of polyhydramnios.
Maternal dehydration does not explain excess fluid.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman at 39 weeks has a frank breech fetus and requests external cephalic version. Which is an absolute contraindication?
clinical_case_questions.e: ECV is offered to suitable patients near term when vaginal birth is otherwise appropriate and emergency caesarean capability is available. Placenta praevia or another contraindication to vaginal birth is a contraindication to ECV.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: placenta praevia requiring caesarean means ECV is not appropriate.
Nulliparity alone is not an absolute contraindication.
Obesity alone is not an absolute contraindication, though it may affect success.
Anterior placenta alone is not an absolute contraindication.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman at 41 weeks has a reassuring CTG and normal fetal movements. Which is the best counselling principle?
o: Discuss induction around/after 41 weeks according to guideline and individual risk
Continue pregnancy indefinitely if CTG is normal
Perform caesarean in every post-dated pregnancy
clinical_case_questions.e: Risks of stillbirth and neonatal morbidity rise with advancing gestation. Discuss induction around 41 weeks according to local guidance and shared decision-making; a reassuring CTG is a snapshot, not a guarantee of future safety.
clinical_case_questions.b: Discuss induction around/after 41 weeks according to guideline and individual risk
optionBuzzwords: Correct: discuss induction at/around 41 weeks per guideline.
A normal CTG does not justify indefinite expectant management.
Post-dates alone does not mandate caesarean.
Tocolysis suppresses contractions and is not appropriate.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 20-year-old requests emergency contraception 72 hours after unprotected intercourse. Which oral option is generally more effective than levonorgestrel later in the 5-day window?
o: Combined oral contraceptive as routine first choice
clinical_case_questions.e: Ulipristal acetate can be used up to 120 hours after intercourse and is generally more effective than levonorgestrel later in the 5-day window. A copper IUD is the most effective emergency contraception when appropriate and available.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: ulipristal is effective up to 120 hours.
Yuzpe combined-pill regimen is less effective and causes more nausea; not preferred when better options are available.
Mifepristone dosing/availability varies and this is not the routine self-directed option.
DMPA is ongoing contraception, not emergency contraception.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with migraine with aura asks for contraception. Which method should generally be avoided because of increased ischaemic stroke risk?
clinical_case_questions.e: Estrogen-containing combined hormonal contraception is contraindicated in migraine with aura because of increased ischaemic stroke risk. Consider progestin-only or non-hormonal methods after assessing other eligibility criteria.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: avoid estrogen-containing combined hormonal contraception in migraine with aura.
Copper IUD is non-hormonal and generally suitable.
LNG-IUS is progestin-only and generally suitable.
Progestin-only pill is generally acceptable if otherwise eligible.

clinical_case_questions.q: A breastfeeding woman at 3 weeks postpartum wants highly effective contraception. Which option is generally appropriate?
o: Progestin-only pill or suitable progestin-only method
Combined estrogen-progestin pill immediately in every patient
clinical_case_questions.e: Progestin-only contraception can generally be initiated early postpartum and is compatible with breastfeeding. Timing and method selection should follow current medical eligibility criteria and individual thrombotic risk.
clinical_case_questions.b: Progestin-only pill or suitable progestin-only method
optionBuzzwords: Correct: progestin-only methods are generally compatible with breastfeeding and early postpartum use.
Combined estrogen-containing methods are restricted early postpartum because of VTE risk and lactation considerations.
Ovulation can precede the first menses; contraception is needed if pregnancy is not desired.
Emergency contraception is not a routine weekly method.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 32-year-old with heavy menstrual bleeding wants long-acting reversible contraception and has no uterine cavity distortion. Which method often reduces menstrual blood loss?
clinical_case_questions.e: The levonorgestrel IUS causes endometrial suppression and often markedly reduces heavy menstrual bleeding; it is a highly effective long-acting reversible contraceptive. Exclude pregnancy and assess cavity/infection risks.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: LNG-IUS often reduces menstrual blood loss.
Copper IUD may increase menstrual bleeding and cramps.
Condoms are useful for STI prevention but are less effective for heavy menstrual bleeding control.
Calendar method does not treat heavy bleeding and is less effective contraception.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 29-year-old with PCOS has BMI 34 kg/m² and is trying to conceive. What is an important first-line intervention alongside fertility assessment?
o: Long-term combined pill while actively trying to conceive
clinical_case_questions.e: Lifestyle modification and weight management improve metabolic health and may restore ovulation in some women with PCOS. For anovulatory infertility, letrozole is commonly first-line pharmacologic ovulation induction when appropriate.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: lifestyle and weight management are foundational.
Oophorectomy causes loss of ovarian function and is not treatment.
Combined pills prevent conception while taken.
Hysterectomy eliminates fertility and is inappropriate.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with PCOS and anovulatory infertility has no other infertility factor. Which drug is commonly recommended first-line for ovulation induction?
clinical_case_questions.e: Letrozole, an aromatase inhibitor, is commonly recommended first-line for ovulation induction in anovulatory infertility due to PCOS, subject to contraindications and local guidance.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: letrozole is preferred first-line in many current guidelines.
Danazol is not used for ovulation induction and may cause androgenic effects.
Tamoxifen is not the routine preferred first-line agent.
GnRH agonist leuprolide suppresses gonadotropins and is not first-line ovulation induction.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman with infertility has a 4-cm submucosal fibroid distorting the uterine cavity. Which treatment may improve fertility when clinically appropriate?
clinical_case_questions.e: Submucosal fibroids that distort the uterine cavity are associated with reduced fertility and may be treated with hysteroscopic myomectomy in selected patients. Treatment depends on size, location, symptoms and reproductive goals.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: hysteroscopic myomectomy can remove cavity-distorting submucosal fibroids.
Endometrial ablation destroys the endometrium and is not appropriate for future fertility.
Salpingectomy removes tubes and worsens natural fertility.
Oophorectomy is not treatment for a fibroid.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 46-year-old with heavy irregular bleeding has a normal pelvic examination. Which is the most appropriate general approach?
o: Evaluate for pregnancy where relevant, structural causes and endometrial pathology based on age/risk
Assume it is menopause and do no evaluation
Order serum CA-125 as the only test
clinical_case_questions.e: AUB evaluation is guided by PALM-COEIN. In women ≥45 years, endometrial sampling is generally indicated; assess pregnancy, anaemia, structural pathology and other causes.
clinical_case_questions.b: Evaluate for pregnancy where relevant, structural causes and endometrial pathology based on age/risk
optionBuzzwords: Correct: evaluate systematically and sample endometrium at age ≥45.
Perimenopause does not exclude endometrial hyperplasia or malignancy.
Anticoagulation can worsen bleeding and is not treatment.
CA-125 is not a diagnostic test for AUB.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 35-year-old with a history of three consecutive first-trimester miscarriages has positive lupus anticoagulant on repeat testing 12 weeks apart. Which pregnancy regimen is commonly used for obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome?
o: No treatment because antibodies are transient
clinical_case_questions.e: For obstetric APS with qualifying pregnancy morbidity and persistent antiphospholipid antibodies, low-dose aspirin plus prophylactic heparin (often LMWH) is commonly used during pregnancy under specialist care. Avoid warfarin during pregnancy.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: aspirin + prophylactic heparin/LMWH is standard for obstetric APS.
Warfarin is teratogenic and generally avoided during pregnancy.
Methotrexate is teratogenic and not treatment for APS.
Persistent antibodies on repeat testing support APS; this is not simply transient positivity.

clinical_case_questions.q: A 28-year-old has recurrent early pregnancy loss and a uterine cavity divided by a midline septum on 3D ultrasound. Which anomaly is associated with recurrent miscarriage and may be treated hysteroscopically in selected patients?
clinical_case_questions.e: A septate uterus is associated with miscarriage and adverse reproductive outcomes. Hysteroscopic septum incision may be considered in selected patients after counselling; distinguish from bicornuate uterus, which has an external fundal cleft.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: septate uterus is the classic cavity anomaly linked to miscarriage.
Bicornuate uterus has a deep external fundal cleft and different management.
Unicornuate uterus is associated with obstetric complications but is not the classic septum.
Arcuate uterus is a mild variant with less clear reproductive impact.

clinical_case_questions.q: A woman has a positive pregnancy test, severe vomiting, ketonuria, dehydration and electrolyte disturbance. What is the initial management priority?
o: IV fluid and electrolyte correction with antiemetics; give thiamine before dextrose if prolonged poor intake
clinical_case_questions.e: Hyperemesis gravidarum requires assessment of dehydration, electrolytes, weight loss and alternative diagnoses. Rehydrate with IV fluids, correct electrolytes and use antiemetics. Give thiamine before dextrose in prolonged vomiting to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy.
clinical_case_questions.b: IV fluid and electrolyte correction with antiemetics; give thiamine before dextrose if prolonged poor intake
optionBuzzwords: Correct: rehydration, electrolyte correction, antiemetics; thiamine before dextrose.
Caesarean has no role in hyperemesis.
Fluid restriction worsens dehydration.
Oxytocin is unrelated.

image_based_questions.q: The CTG shows recurrent decelerations whose nadir occurs after the peak of each uterine contraction. What is the pattern?
image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: The decelerations begin after the contraction starts and recover after it ends, with nadir after the contraction peak: late decelerations, suggesting uteroplacental insufficiency. Assess the whole trace and maternal-fetal context; initiate intrauterine resuscitative measures and expedite birth if persistent pathological CTG.
image_based_questions.b: Late deceleration → contraction peak precedes FHR nadir; uteroplacental insufficiency.
optionBuzzwords: Early: mirror contractions; head compression.
Correct: delayed onset/nadir/recovery; uteroplacental insufficiency.
Variable: abrupt V/W-shaped drops; cord compression.
Sinusoidal: smooth regular sine-wave baseline, severe fetal anaemia/hypoxia association.

o: Slow progress requiring reassessment and action according to protocol

The exact modern labour-management thresholds vary by guideline; do not use the chart in isolation.
image_based_questions.b: Partograph action line crossed → reassess labour and intervene/referral as appropriate.
optionBuzzwords: Normal progress remains on/left of the alert/action trajectory.
Correct: crossing action line prompts reassessment and action per protocol.
Second stage begins at full cervical dilatation.
Partograph cervical progress does not diagnose fetal demise.

image_based_questions.q: A first-trimester ultrasound image is represented by diffuse echogenic vesicular material without a normal embryo. Beta-hCG is markedly elevated. Most likely diagnosis?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Schematic snowstorm appearance of complete mole" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="25" width="650" height="280" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><path d="M360 48 C270 45 190 90 180 170 C170 245 250 275 360 278 C470 275 550 245 540 170 C530 90 450 45 360 48Z" fill="#27364b" stroke="#9fb4cc" stroke-width="4"/><g fill="#dbeafe"><circle cx="280" cy="110" r="9"/><circle cx="330" cy="90" r="7"/><circle cx="380" cy="115" r="12"/><circle cx="430" cy="95" r="8"/><circle cx="250" cy="160" r="8"/><circle cx="300" cy="170" r="13"/><circle cx="350" cy="145" r="8"/><circle cx="405" cy="165" r="10"/><circle cx="465" cy="155" r="9"/><circle cx="270" cy="215" r="11"/><circle cx="330" cy="225" r="7"/><circle cx="390" cy="210" r="13"/><circle cx="445" cy="225" r="8"/><circle cx="355" cy="185" r="6"/><circle cx="220" cy="190" r="6"/><circle cx="490" cy="195" r="7"/></g><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Diffuse echogenic vesicular pattern (schematic)</text></svg>

image_based_questions.e: A diffuse “snowstorm”/cluster-of-grapes appearance with very high hCG and absent normal embryo is classic for complete hydatidiform mole. Confirm by ultrasound and manage with suction evacuation and serial hCG surveillance.
image_based_questions.b: Complete mole → snowstorm appearance + very high β-hCG.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: complete mole has diffuse hydropic villi and no embryo.
Missed miscarriage may show a nonviable gestational sac but not the classic diffuse vesicular pattern.
Ectopic pregnancy is extrauterine; assess adnexa/free fluid.
Placenta accreta is abnormal placental invasion later in pregnancy.

image_based_questions.q: A woman with positive β-hCG has an empty uterine cavity. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an extrauterine adnexal ring with peripheral vascularity. What is the most likely diagnosis?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Schematic adnexal ring-of-fire sign" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="25" width="650" height="280" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><ellipse cx="360" cy="165" rx="180" ry="105" fill="#24364c" stroke="#9fb4cc" stroke-width="4"/><ellipse cx="360" cy="165" rx="90" ry="55" fill="#101827" stroke="#f59e0b" stroke-width="16"/><ellipse cx="360" cy="165" rx="48" ry="27" fill="#334155" stroke="#f8fafc" stroke-width="3"/><circle cx="360" cy="165" r="10" fill="#f8fafc"/><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Adnexal ring-of-fire sign (schematic)</text></svg>
image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: An adnexal gestational sac/ring separate from the ovary in a patient with positive hCG and empty uterus strongly suggests ectopic pregnancy. “Ring of fire” vascularity is not specific and may also be seen around a corpus luteum; interpret anatomy and clinical context.
image_based_questions.b: Positive hCG + empty uterus + extraovarian adnexal ring → ectopic pregnancy until excluded.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: extraovarian adnexal ring in this context suggests tubal ectopic.
Corpus luteum can show peripheral flow but is within the ovary; not an ectopic gestation.
Endometrioma has ground-glass internal echoes, not gestational ring.
Fibroid is a solid myometrial lesion.

image_based_questions.q: The ultrasound schematic shows placental tissue covering the internal cervical os. Which clinical precaution is essential in a patient with antepartum bleeding?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Placenta praevia covering internal os" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="20" width="650" height="285" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><path d="M245 55 Q360 15 475 55 L510 250 Q360 300 210 250Z" fill="#e2e8f0" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M270 75 Q360 35 450 75 L465 150 Q360 185 255 150Z" fill="#b45309" stroke="#fbbf24" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M300 170 Q360 140 420 170 L405 250 Q360 275 315 250Z" fill="#64748b" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M285 165 L435 165" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="8"/><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Placental tissue reaches the internal os (schematic)</text></svg>
image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
o: Avoid digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia is excluded
image_based_questions.e: Placenta praevia is diagnosed by ultrasound. Avoid digital vaginal examination until placental location is known because it may provoke severe haemorrhage. Stabilise and plan delivery according to placental location, bleeding and gestation.
image_based_questions.b: Placenta praevia → painless bleeding; no digital PV exam before localisation.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: digital examination can trigger catastrophic bleeding.
Digital examination is contraindicated until praevia is excluded.
Fundal pressure is unsafe and not diagnostic.
Unsupervised induction is unsafe.

image_based_questions.q: Ultrasound schematic shows multiple well-defined solid lesions arising from the myometrium in a patient with heavy menstrual bleeding. Most likely diagnosis?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Schematic uterine leiomyomas" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="20" width="650" height="285" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><path d="M270 55 Q360 25 450 55 Q485 130 455 255 Q360 295 265 255 Q235 130 270 55Z" fill="#334155" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="4"/><circle cx="360" cy="145" r="62" fill="#64748b" stroke="#fbbf24" stroke-width="8"/><circle cx="280" cy="205" r="28" fill="#64748b" stroke="#fbbf24" stroke-width="6"/><circle cx="430" cy="220" r="20" fill="#64748b" stroke="#fbbf24" stroke-width="5"/><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Multiple well-defined myometrial masses (schematic)</text></svg>
image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: Leiomyomas are well-circumscribed benign smooth-muscle tumours arising from myometrium. They may be submucosal, intramural or subserosal; submucosal lesions most strongly affect bleeding/fertility.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: multiple well-defined myometrial masses are fibroids.
Adenomyosis causes diffuse myometrial heterogeneity and globular uterus.
Endometrial hyperplasia thickens endometrium, not discrete myometrial masses.
Cervical polyp is a focal cervical canal lesion.

image_based_questions.q: A cystic ovarian lesion shows homogeneous low-level “ground-glass” echoes in a woman with dysmenorrhoea and infertility. What is the likely diagnosis?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Schematic ovarian endometrioma ultrasound" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="20" width="650" height="285" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><ellipse cx="360" cy="165" rx="155" ry="105" fill="#334155" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="5"/><g fill="#64748b" opacity=".85"><circle cx="285" cy="130" r="15"/><circle cx="330" cy="110" r="22"/><circle cx="380" cy="135" r="18"/><circle cx="425" cy="155" r="25"/><circle cx="315" cy="185" r="27"/><circle cx="370" cy="205" r="22"/><circle cx="415" cy="205" r="14"/><circle cx="265" cy="180" r="12"/></g><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Homogeneous low-level internal echoes (schematic)</text></svg>
image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: An endometrioma classically shows homogeneous low-level ground-glass echoes due to chronic blood products. Correlate with symptoms and assess atypical features.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: ground-glass echoes are characteristic of endometrioma.
Simple cyst is typically anechoic with thin wall and posterior enhancement.
Dermoid often contains echogenic fat/calcification and shadowing.
Serous cystadenoma is usually simple or multilocular fluid-filled, not ground-glass.

image_based_questions.q: The ovarian ultrasound schematic shows increased ovarian volume and multiple small follicles arranged peripherally. In a woman with oligomenorrhoea and hirsutism, what is the likely diagnosis?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Schematic polycystic ovarian morphology" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="20" width="650" height="285" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><ellipse cx="360" cy="165" rx="190" ry="115" fill="#334155" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="4"/><g fill="#0f172a" stroke="#93c5fd" stroke-width="3"><circle cx="230" cy="130" r="12"/><circle cx="275" cy="100" r="14"/><circle cx="320" cy="90" r="11"/><circle cx="365" cy="95" r="13"/><circle cx="410" cy="100" r="12"/><circle cx="455" cy="125" r="13"/><circle cx="480" cy="170" r="12"/><circle cx="445" cy="210" r="14"/><circle cx="390" cy="230" r="12"/><circle cx="335" cy="230" r="13"/><circle cx="280" cy="205" r="12"/><circle cx="245" cy="170" r="11"/></g><ellipse cx="360" cy="165" rx="65" ry="45" fill="#64748b" opacity=".5"/><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Multiple small peripheral follicles (schematic)</text></svg>

image_based_questions.e: Polycystic ovarian morphology can support PCOS when combined with ovulatory dysfunction and/or hyperandrogenism after excluding mimics. Ultrasound morphology alone does not diagnose PCOS.
image_based_questions.b: Oligo-ovulation + hyperandrogenism ± polycystic ovarian morphology → PCOS.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: clinical features plus morphology support PCOS after exclusion of mimics.
POI usually has elevated FSH and low ovarian reserve.
Torsion is an acute painful enlarged ovary, often with peripheral follicles/oedema, not chronic endocrine syndrome.
Dermoid is a focal complex mass with fat/calcification.

image_based_questions.q: A cervical cytology smear schematic shows atypical squamous cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and hyperchromatic nuclei. Which category is most concerning?

image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: HSIL indicates high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion and carries significant risk of CIN2/3. Prompt colposcopy with biopsy or guideline-based expedited management is required.
image_based_questions.b: HSIL → high-grade cytology → colposcopy/biopsy or guideline-based expedited treatment.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: high N:C ratio and hyperchromasia are compatible with HSIL.
ASC-US is equivocal atypia, not a high-grade category.
Normal cells have low N:C ratio and uniform nuclei.
Atrophy may mimic atypia but requires clinical/cytological correlation.

image_based_questions.q: Histology schematic shows a glomerulus-like Schiller–Duval body. Which serum tumour marker is most likely elevated?

image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: Schiller–Duval bodies are characteristic of yolk sac (endodermal sinus) tumour, which commonly secretes AFP.
image_based_questions.b: Schiller–Duval body → yolk sac tumour → ↑ AFP.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: AFP is the characteristic marker.
LDH is associated with dysgerminoma.
Inhibin is associated with granulosa-cell tumours.
CA-125 may be raised in epithelial ovarian malignancy but is not the classic marker here.

image_based_questions.q: A woman with two previous caesarean deliveries has placenta praevia. Imaging suggests placental tissue invading the myometrium with loss of the normal interface. Which condition is suspected?
image_based_questions.image: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 330" role="img" aria-label="Schematic placenta accreta spectrum" style="width:100%;height:auto;background:#f7f9fc;border-radius:12px"><rect x="35" y="20" width="650" height="285" rx="12" fill="#101827"/><path d="M230 45 Q360 15 490 45 L470 270 Q360 300 250 270Z" fill="#334155" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="4"/><path d="M260 65 Q360 35 460 65 L450 135 Q360 165 270 135Z" fill="#b45309" stroke="#fbbf24" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M275 145 Q360 175 445 145 L430 240 Q360 270 290 240Z" fill="#64748b" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M300 130 Q360 180 420 130 M330 145 Q360 210 390 145" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="8" fill="none"/><text x="360" y="320" font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#cbd5e1" font-weight="400" text-anchor="middle">Abnormal placental invasion into myometrium (schematic)</text></svg>
image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: Placenta accreta spectrum results from abnormal placental adherence/invasion, with risk increased by placenta praevia and previous caesarean scars. Plan delivery in a specialist centre with blood products and multidisciplinary team.
image_based_questions.b: Placenta praevia + prior caesarean + abnormal myometrial invasion → placenta accreta spectrum.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: risk factors and imaging suggest PAS.
Abruption is premature separation of normally implanted placenta.
Vasa praevia involves fetal vessels over/near the internal os.
Circumvallate placenta is an extrachorial placental morphology, not invasive placentation.

image_based_questions.q: The fetus is longitudinal with the buttocks presenting at the pelvic inlet and hips flexed, knees extended. What is the presentation?

image_based_questions.imageSource: Original MEDSHUBH schematic illustration (not a patient photograph).
image_based_questions.e: Frank breech: hips flexed and knees extended, with buttocks presenting. Complete breech has hips and knees flexed; footling has one or both feet presenting.
image_based_questions.b: Frank breech: hips flexed, knees extended.
optionBuzzwords: Correct: hips flexed, knees extended = frank breech.
Complete breech: hips and knees flexed.
Footling breech: one/both feet are the presenting part.
Cephalic: head presents.
